messages:
Maya: quick thread — sketching a proposal for how on-prem agents should handle staged activation and revocation signals for artifact upgrades. want feedback on interface boundaries and failure modes.

Sam: high level +1. main tradeoff i see is how much throttling/holdback we give local ops vs central control. do we let agents autonomously revoke based on signed revocation lists or require a pull-confirmation? :thinking_face:

Liam: leaning toward signed revocation lists that agents fetch and validate locally. central control signs both activation manifests and revocation deltas. agent policy decides enforcement (auto-revoke, notify-only, quarantine). avoids central availability dependence for safety. :+1:

Olivia: agree, but need clear semantics for "activation window" vs "grace period". if we revoke a model mid-rollout we must ensure no in-flight state corruption (KV cache, checkpoints). propose: activation signal = "go-live" timestamp + signature. revoke signal = explicit hash in revocation-set with signed epoch. agent rules: do not garbage collect previous artifacts until grace_end = revoke_ts + GC_DELAY.

Sam: what about rollback/compat? if new artifact schema incompatible, we need a compatible fallback that can be automatically reactivated. suggests we track compatibility-metadata in manifest and route fallback policy per service.

Maya: proto manifest snippet i had in mind:

```
manifest_version: 1
entries:
  - id: services/llm/runtime
    hash: sha256:ab12cdef...
    activate_after: 2026-04-06T00:00:00Z
    activation_signature: sig:BASE64...
    compatibility: { api: v2, kv_cache_format: v1 }
revocation_set:
  epoch: 42
  revoked_hashes: [ sha256:deadbeef... ]
  signed_by: key://redwood-cp/rotation-2026
```

Liam: nice. couple interface suggestions:
- agent should expose a single endpoint for control-plane polling: GET /agent/v1/activation?since=epoch_n
- control plane returns compact bundle (manifest + sig + revocation_set). agent validates signature via configured root key (KMS/HSM)
- agent emits audit event: activation_applied, activation_skipped(reason), revocation_applied

Olivia: +1. also require signed attestations for post-activation health: agent runs smoke checks and posts a signed health attestation back. if health fails repeatedly, control plane can mark as auto-rollforward=false and admins get pager.

Sam: how do we handle air-gapped sites with long offline windows? must support distribution via signed tarball + index and ability to stage activations without immediate CP ping. maybe add an "activation-token" that expires and can be distributed out-of-band.

Maya: agree. plan: allow offline activation by embedding signed activation credentials in the bundle. agent verifies signatures and checks local time vs activate_after. we should document expected clock skew allowances and require monotonic counters in revocation_set epochs to prevent replay.

deploy-bot: NOTICE: last signed control-plane key rotation detected at epoch 2026-03-15T12:00Z (rotated-by: olivia). Ensure agents have updated root keys before next activation window.

Liam: big open question — garbage collection policy. i propose tiers: keep N previous artifacts for immediate rollback, keep older artifacts in archival storage (optional), and never GC artifacts referenced by any active manifest/revocation window. GC only after manual admin confirmation or after archival retention period.

Olivia: ops concerns: signed revocations are powerful — need a tamper-evidence timeline and audit log export for customer compliance. include per-agent signed checkpoints with proof-of-apply.

Maya: proposed action items:
- draft RFC with manifest schema + agent API + signature validation flow (owner: maya)
- add revocation_set monotonic epoch semantics and sample code (owner: liam)
- offline activation mode doc + clock skew guidance (owner: sam)
- audit/attestation payload spec (owner: olivia)

Sam: sg, i'll spin up a short doc and drop a follow-up PR.

Olivia: i'll prep notes for compliance on retention and audit export.

Liam: i'll prototype the endpoint and a small validator lib we can embed in the agent.

Maya: thanks — if anyone has strong objections speak now, otherwise i'll create the RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. :eyes:
